decisions.rationale: Basis: ops-reconciler-loop5 on a scratch copy of the frozen export at c3e666bf (lab.json sha256 4968154e, tests/lab.mjs 7403eb2f, tests/behavior.mjs 1411ab6f, tests/service_behavior.py bfec51d8); npm run setup in tests (npm ci plus a Python 3.14.6 .venv with the 14 pins), Node v24.2.0, bash 3.2.57, macOS arm64; every run under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT. The shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result and count lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. The reconciler's solution (main.py and ci.yml written by the reconciler from the README and topic pages; compose.yaml, decisions.yaml and the Dockerfile copied from the SME critic's solution, since no finding contests them) passes 26/26 and its lines equal expected/solved-summary.txt; 30 one-change variants of it were run (variants-out.txt in the reconciler folder). Not run: Windows, Linux, a real Python 3.10, a real docker binary; GitHub, pflag and PyPI pages were not re-retrieved, so claims resting on them cite the critics' dated retrievals. Valid, high (same defect as ops-sme-r5-01; one change resolves both). Reproduced: pip install --dry-run --only-binary=:all: --python-version 3.10 --platform manylinux2014_x86_64 -r tests/requirements.txt stops with 'No matching distribution found for annotated-doc==0.0.7' ('0.0.7 Requires-Python >=3.11'); the same command for 3.11 resolves all 14 pins. Installed METADATA: starlette 1.10.0 and annotated-doc 0.0.7 say Requires-Python >=3.11, fastapi 0.136.3 says >=3.10. README line 45, lab.json prerequisites and setup_python.mjs line 23 all admit 3.10, so the stated prerequisite is false (lab-contract section 10: prerequisites are verified). Stale-venv trap reproduced: a .venv created by python3.11 --without-pip is reused by setup_python.mjs (line 29 creates only when the venv's python is missing) and setup exits 1 with 'No module named pip' without recreating it. Required minimal change: (1) raise the floor to Python 3.11 in README line 45, the troubleshooting line, lab.json prerequisites and setup_python.mjs (minor >= 11 and the message); this is preferred because it changes no pin and the image itself runs Python 3.14 (starter/reviews/Dockerfile line 6). Repinning starlette/annotated-doc to 3.10-capable versions is an acceptable alternative only if a 3.10 dry-run then resolves and tests 24-26 still pass. (2) setup_python.mjs checks an existing .venv's interpreter version and that pip imports, and recreates .venv when either fails. (3) one troubleshooting line: if setup fails after changing Python, delete .venv and run npm run setup again. Recheck: the 3.10 dry-run no longer contradicts the stated floor; a venv below the floor or without pip is recreated by npm run setup; starter and solved summaries unchanged.

Ruling principle (loop 5C instruction): earlier enumerated lists (S1-S14, q1/q2, g1-g7/f1-f8, c/b lists, H1-H9) are evidence of plausible learner shapes, not a binding allowlist. Each finding is judged on whether the behaviour judged matches the README objective, whether a plausible correct solution is falsely rejected or a real leak, missing limit, unforwarded token or wrong mapping is falsely accepted, and whether the message is true and non-revealing. Valid, medium (part 1 is the same defect as ops-sme-r5-03; part 2 is separate). Reproduced: the README-literal httpx.Timeout(connect=2.0, read=3.0) written inside the handler scores 23/26; test 24 says the service 'made no HTTPX call to the shop api ... call the api with httpx, as the starter does', test 25 'never called the shop api: make the call', test 26 'never called it ... make the call to the shop api with httpx'. The same constructor at module level gets 'could not be loaded: ValueError: httpx.Timeout must either include a default, or set all four parameters explicitly.' Hard-coding http://api:8080 instead of API_BASE_URL scores 23/26 with the same three no-call messages although the stand-in recorded the call. Rejection is correct in both (the code is broken, and README phase 4 plus the compose rule require API_BASE_URL), but the messages direct the learner to add a call they already wrote, so they are not true guidance for that state. Required minimal change: (1) service_behavior.py records, per scenario, the type and text of an exception that escaped the handler (for example raise_server_exceptions=True inside the existing try, keeping type name and message, truncated), and lab.mjs reports 'the handler raised <Type>: <text> before calling the shop api' when no shop call was made and an exception was recorded; (2) when outgoing requests exist but none starts with API_BASE_URL, the message names the URL called and says to build it from API_BASE_URL; the no-call wording stays only for code that made no HTTPX request and raised nothing. No README hint of the constructor form (ops-edu-11 forbids it). Recheck: both variants fail the same tests with the new true messages; the shipped starter and checkpoint messages are unchanged except as ops-edu-r5-04 requires.

Reproduced on the shipped starter run: test 24 prints the all-limits-off branch of tests/lab.mjs line 240 (its main clause and its parenthetical). The starter passes timeout=None, so this prints in phase 1, before phase 5 asks the worksheet field service_calls.httpx_with_timeout_none (decisions.yaml line 66). Both the phrase 'ran with no limits at all' and the parenthetical describe the behaviour that field asks about, which breaks the loop-2 acceptance under ops-edu-r1-01 (no starter-run or checkpoint-run message states an item's expected option) and the ops-edu-11 proviso (no reworded timeout message singles out a worksheet option). The value is not repeated here. Required minimal change: reword the whole all-limits-off branch (lab.mjs line 240), not only the parenthetical, so that it states only what the grader observed in terms that do not describe a client's behaviour against a hung api, points to the page's timeout rule, and gives the required 2-second connect and 3-second read limits. The wording must be true for any code that reaches that branch (the grader sees recorded limits, not source), so it must not assert that the code passes timeout=None. The 5-second-default branch (line 241) prints only after a learner edit and may stay. Recheck: the starter and end-of-S38 checkpoint messages are swept again and none states or rules out an option of any worksheet item; expected/starter-summary.txt is unchanged (titles only).
